name: Scrub top
definition: Loose pullover top of woven or stretch-woven fabric with a V-neck or crew neck, short sleeves and patch pockets, worn as a medical or care uniform; scrub trousers are work pants.
reason: Uniform filed by form (rule 3); no top kind has this form; ten scrub makers compared in GD/REG (C2(a)). Tunic shirt definition should exclude it.

name: Lab coat (white coat)
definition: Knee-length or longer button-front work coat of white or coloured cotton or polyester, worn over clothing in laboratories, clinics and workshops; splash or chemical rating is an attribute.
reason: Workwear and light protective clothing are A1 (step 17); below hip, so coats leaf; no coat kind fits; Medelita, Adar sell them apart.

name: Fur coat (shuba)
definition: Coat made of fur pelts or faux fur worn pile-out (mink, fox, sable or faux fur coat); fur type is an attribute; fur-trimmed or fur-lined coats and suede-out sheepskin coats are filed by cut.
reason: Second stated material-is-form exception (pelt construction, like fleece); CNPP ranks fur-apparel makers (C2(a)); ten makers make only fur coats.

name: Raincoat (mac)
definition: Coat ending below the hip of waterproof, rubberised, coated or water-repellent fabric made to keep off rain, without the trench coat's belt, epaulettes and storm flap; a hip-length rain jacket is the shell jacket.
reason: Shell jacket is hip length and trench coat belted; Gannex, Alligator, Sanyo raincoats had no home; length rule puts it in coats.

name: Co-ord set
definition: Matching top and bottom (trousers, shorts or skirt) cut from the same fabric or print and sold together as one outfit; a tailored jacket set is the business suit, a long-tunic set the tunic suit; tracksuits are filed by their pieces (R-84).
reason: Sold as one outfit category; leaf A1.3.1 already holds two-piece sets (tunic suit, lehenga choli); pieces sold apart keep their kinds.

name: Casual jacket (blouson)
definition: Sleeved jacket ending at the hip or above, worn over other clothing and fastened at the front, in a cut no other jacket kind covers (blouson, short or cropped jacket, leather or suede jacket not cut for riding); cut and material are attributes.
reason: Ten GD makers show only plain jackets; no jacket kind is generic; shorts and skirt show broad kinds are allowed (C2(a)).

name: Team jersey
definition: Pullover top in a team's colours and badges, of knitted jersey or mesh, with or without a collar, sold as a team, replica, retro or fan shirt (football, rugby, hockey, basketball); a cycling jersey is E2.
reason: Key keeps team and fan jerseys in A1; GR has a jerseys leaf; Castore, Galex, ABM, Icarus FC, Rasan make only kits.

candidate: firefighter protective clothing (turnout gear, proximity suit)
name: Firefighter suit (turnout gear)
definition: Protective coat-and-trousers set or one-piece suit with flame-, heat- and water-resistant layers worn by firefighters, aluminised proximity suits included; hazard rating is an attribute.
reason: PPE is A1 by step 17 and filed by form; sold as suits like the bee suit; CNPP ranks firefighter-clothing makers.

name: Braces (suspenders)
definition: Pair of straps worn over the shoulders and clipped or buttoned to the trousers to hold them up; stocking suspenders (garters) are hosiery accessories, not this kind.
reason: Worn waist accessory with no A1.7 home (belt is round the waist); Albert Thurston, HoldUp, French bretelles makers sell them apart.
